The owner counted the hours

She wasn't losing coaches. She was losing their mornings.

https://mojowaylife.com/stories/161-the-owner-counted-the-hours.html
linkedin:
The owner runs a studio with forty coaches and a retention problem she couldn't name. It wasn't churn. Coaches stayed. Clients stayed, mostly.

What she found, when she actually counted, was that a coach's day was shaped by writing: session notes, progress emails, the report that was supposed to be sent a week ago and wasn't.

Each of those tasks was small. Together they were eating the part of the day when the coach was at their best.

Her maths was blunt. If a coach spends forty minutes preparing each in-person review, and they do six a week, that's four hours. Four hours is one client. Twelve clients a month, across forty coaches.

The fix wasn't more discipline, or another spreadsheet. It was removing the writing bottleneck so the coach could spend the hour on the person instead of on the paperwork.

Buying a tool is a strange way to buy back time, and that's what it is.

MOJOWAY's body kit turns the scan into a page in minutes, with the coach's own note on top. The studio's gain is the hour the coach doesn't spend assembling it.
